sections.text: You packed lunch for a pullout by the creek. Your passenger was picturing lunch at an actual table. Better to find that out in the driveway than after forty minutes of gravel.
Trade one want and one limit

Try ‘I’d like to get away from the highway, but I want to be back before dinner.’ Then let the other person go. A restroom, a shorter stretch on rough road, or a place where someone can comfortably get out of the car is part of the plan, not a footnote.
Pick a stop that fits both answers. If it doesn’t exist on this route, change the route. The point of taking the back way isn’t to make somebody endure it.
Share the map before you move
If your passenger wants to navigate, agree on the next useful landmark and the route back to pavement while parked.
sections.after: covers what to save ahead of time. Nobody has to take a shift with the map; set up the route while stopped if they’d rather look out the window.

sections.text: Missed a turn? Keep going to a safe, legal place to stop. An extra mile is easier to undo than a sudden maneuver.
Both people can call a stop
‘Next safe stop, please’ is enough. There’s no need to make a case for a stretch or some quiet.
sections.after: starts with picking a place that keeps the road and its entrances clear.

sections.text: Check in at the first stop
Ask one real question: more gravel, a shorter loop, or home?
Give the answer time. Don’t ask with the engine already running.
Set the next leg together while parked. If the shorter option wins, take it without keeping score.
Sometimes you end up at a picnic table closer to town. You still get to eat lunch together.
